title: A week in Lunceford's band under Eddie Wilcox
summary: He sat in for a sick Simeon for a week in a Bronx theatre with the Lunceford band then led by pianist Wilcox, which was the whole show.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Now, you also did a week with Jimmy Lunceford at one
Holmes (12/5) - 66
time, about this time, too. That's before you got the steady day job.

Yeah. I just sat in for somebody. Let me see, Willie Smith had just left the band or something. I don't know who that was. No, I was in Simeon's place. Simeon used to be in the band. Simeon, I think, was sick. He had taken sick. And they had to open at this theatre up in the Bronx. So the piano player, Wilcox, he asked me could I make the week with them. So it was all right with me as far as I'm concerned. So I made the week. You know, no big deal about that. It was just a week, just like you said. That was all of that.
Because I guess Wilcox had taken over the band at that time.
Yeah, he was in charge.
I remember one of our Winter Carnivals at Hamilton College about 1950, I would say, Eddie Wilcox's band was hired, and Simeon was in that band.
Yeah.
Because I remember I recognized him.
Yeah, Simeon... Well, yeah, he was a regular member of the band, yeah.
And you remember that Joe Thomas was on tenor.
Yes.
Holmes (12/5) - 67
And Earl Carruthers on baritone.
Yes.
Was the band the featured thing there, or was that a show also?
No, no, this was a band feature. They were the whole show. I mean, they was doing their act. We didn't play nothin' for nobody else.
Did the public dance?
No. The band was the show.
So they came to hear the band.
Yeah.
Did you solo any on that?
No! Solo? Me?
Well, were you the only alto?
No, I couldn't have been in a band that size. But I don't know who the other alto was. I don't know. I don't remember.
